_notes: Taito do Brasil, 1980-1985: 8080 CPU, 2KB ROMs at 0x0000 (three to five of them), 512 bytes of scratch RAM at 0x3E00
and the 256-byte battery-backed window at 0x4000 that PinMAME's taito driver saves as the .nv file.
The display DMA (0x4080-0x408F) and command DMA (0x4090-0x409F) sit inside that window, so player scores,
ball in play and credits are in the .nv image. Little-endian: the display holds each 6-digit score as three
BCD bytes least-significant first; the stored high score at 0x4079 is most-significant first (endian: big).
